messages.author: 61052ee250cd6ec8
messages.subject: POSIXct and plyr/ddply
parts:
Hello all,

I found what seems to be a bug when using ddply where one of the
variables in my data frame is a POSIXct class and the rest are not.
My data.frame has a column of IDs (factor), a column of times, and a
column of numeric values. I'm looking to get the value at the
earliest time value for each ID.

To generate the data:

t1 <- as.POSIXct("2010-01-01 10:10:10")
t2 <- as.POSIXct("2010-03-01 10:10:10")
d <- data.frame(id=factor(sample(1:5,100, replace=TRUE)),
datetime=rep(seq(t1, t2, length.out=10)),
value=rnorm(100))

> head(d)
id datetime value
1 1 2010-01-01 10:10:10 -0.5181354
2 2 2010-01-07 23:30:10 0.7973425
3 4 2010-01-14 12:50:10 0.9312029
4 5 2010-01-21 02:10:10 -0.4238824
5 4 2010-01-27 15:30:10 1.6215834
6 2 2010-02-03 04:50:10 -0.7078981


Then run ddply on it to return the start time, min.val and then a new
value set to 4 (just as a bit of a sanity check)

dd <- ddply(d, .(id), function(x){c(start=min(x$datetime), min.val=x
$value[which.min(x$datetime)], constant=4)})

> head(dd)
id start min.val constant
1 1 2010-01-01 10:10:10 1969-12-31 18:59:59 1969-12-31 19:00:04
2 2 2010-01-01 10:10:10 1969-12-31 19:00:00 1969-12-31 19:00:04
3 3 2010-01-01 10:10:10 1969-12-31 18:59:59 1969-12-31 19:00:04
4 4 2010-01-01 10:10:10 1969-12-31 19:00:01 1969-12-31 19:00:04
5 5 2010-01-01 10:10:10 1969-12-31 19:00:00 1969-12-31 19:00:04


It looks like I can recover the ideal values with as.numeric, but it
doesn't seem like I should have to.

If there's something I'm doing wrong please let me know, but it seems
correct on my end.

Thanks,
Adam

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: POSIXct and plyr/ddply
parts:
The problem is that you're using c(), which forces all elements to be
the same type. Use data.frame or the summarise helper:

dd <- ddply(d, .(id), summarise,
start = min(datetime),
min.val=value[which.min(datetime)],
constant=4)

Hadley
